geometry_edits.rationale: Moderate the bend so the dominant mass remains continuous but less compressed and more programmatically legible.
Increase the cantilevered reach to produce a clearer lifted ground condition and threshold.
Open the courtyard toward the access edge to make the void public-facing and program-aligned.
Enlarge the court so the subtraction reads as occupied public space rather than a trim cut.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the dominant gesture into a clearer continuous longitudinal arc that can organize the street building and improve silhouette continuity.
Reduce the over-stepped feel so the main mass reads as one legible body rather than a clipped stack.
Extend the lifted portion to create a more legible ground response at the frontage and a clearer public edge.
Align the courtyard opening to the verified access side so the void becomes a public threshold rather than an internal subtraction.
Increase void presence enough to become a meaningful usable court and improve publicness.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent compact mass in all four views, but the dominant gesture is still a generic stepped block with a weakly expressed public void. The parcel is respected, yet the mass mostly fills it instead of organizing a compelling open-space figure. The verified access edge is not convincingly answered: the visible ground condition remains largely sealed, with no clear seam, undercut, or court oriented to the frontage. Sectionally, the stepped/canted upper form does not yet produce a strong neighborhood-living hierarchy or an especially useful public threshold. It is therefore repairable but not program-fit enough to pass as-is.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact commercial massing can preserve a clear ground threshold while keeping the upper volume calm and legible.
A courtyard-like void can be a true social interior, not just a subtraction, if it is visibly occupied by the building edge.
A small neighborhood venue benefits from direct ground contact and a simple, readable enclosure around shared space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Scale and typology skew toward high-rise office rather than neighborhood living.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A stacked/tower-like mass can create a strong ground datum, but this reference is much more vertical and not a close program fit.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual reference; useful for public-threshold strategy, but its pedestrian-bridge typology is not the same building use.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A bridged or elevated gesture can protect an open ground plane when the program wants permeability.

warnings: Access response is semantically weak relative to the verified frontage edge.
Void is present only as a minor internalized condition, not as a legible public threshold.
Stepped silhouette is coherent, but still reads more like mass trimming than a program-driven section.
No strong evidence of an active ground edge for neighborhood living.
